week.weeklyOverview: Preschool Community Helpers goes deeper than toddler imitation play: children map real neighborhood helpers, interview guest helpers (or teacher-in-role), match tools to jobs, and run richer dramatic-play centers (clinic, mail, kitchen, block city). Emphasize gratitude, safety helpers, and many kinds of work—including caregivers and educators. Keep props sturdy and roles flexible so every child can help.
week.weeklyMaterials: Helper hats/vests (optional); doctor kit; play food; mailbags/envelopes; clipboards; safe plastic tools; community map poster or teacher-drawn map; toy phones; helper picture cards; thank-you card materials; blocks for community city; obstacle-course cones; name badges for interview circle.
week.teacherPreparation: Stage centers before arrival and preview one open-ended Community Helpers invitation; step back so children lead.
week.familyConnection: We are learning about community helpers—people who keep neighborhoods safe, healthy, and caring. Ask your child: “Who helps in our neighborhood?” You may share a helper you know (nurse, driver, cook, teacher, custodian) for our thank-you chart. No costume required for Career Day energy—curiosity counts.
milestones: Language: Names helper roles and tools; uses thank-you language and interview questions.
SEL: Practices gratitude, cooperative roles, and flexible turn-taking in dramatic play.
Cognition: Matches tools to jobs; reads simple map symbols; compares helper roles.
Motor: Moves through rescue relay/obstacle course; uses fine motor for mail, charts, and cards.
Creativity: Builds community block cities and invents helper stories in dramatic play.

printableIdeas.title: Our Community Map (Blank Neighborhood)
printableIdeas.purpose: Simple map template for Community Map Talk—children add stickers/drawings of helpers and places (school, clinic, store, park).

printableIdeas.title: Helper Interview Question Cards
printableIdeas.purpose: Picture-supported questions (What tools help you? How do you stay safe?) for Helper Interview Circle.

printableIdeas.title: Thank-You Helper Mini Card
printableIdeas.purpose: Half-page card for Thank-You Card Workshop; children draw a helper and dictate a thank-you message.

songs.title: Helpers All Around (LLH Chant)
songs.motions: March in place; show hands on “helper’s hands”; tip an imaginary hat on thank-you; point outward on “everywhere.”
songs.teacherDirections: Primary theme song—use instead of any modern neighborhood pop song. Invite children to insert a helper they know. Keep verses optional; two choruses are enough.
songs.suggestedPace: Steady march tempo; clap on thank-you lines.
songs.transitionPurpose: Introduces helper vocabulary and gratitude language.
songs.lyrics:
Helpers, helpers, all around—
In our home and in our town.
Who can help? Let's look and see—
A helper's hands can care for me!

Doctor, teacher, driver, cook,
Mail friends bringing letters—look!
Firefighter, builder, nurse who cares—
Helpers help us everywhere.

Thank you, thank you, helpers true,
We can be good helpers too.
Kind hands ready, hearts so wide—
Community helpers side by side!

songs.title: Hurry, Hurry, Drive the Fire Truck
songs.motions: Steering motions; climbing hands; spray hose; slow march back. Offer seated steering for mixed mobility.
songs.teacherDirections: Pair with Firefighter Rescue Relay. Emphasize safety helpers who practice—not scary emergencies. Keep “fire” pretend and calm.
songs.whenToUse: Before firefighter play or outdoor relay.
songs.suggestedPace: Fast for hurry verses; slow for return verse.
songs.transitionPurpose: Energizes bodies and sets firefighter role play.
songs.lyrics:
Hurry, hurry, drive the fire truck,
Hurry, hurry, drive the fire truck,
Hurry, hurry, drive the fire truck,
Ding, ding, ding, ding, ding!

Hurry, hurry, climb the ladder…
Hurry, hurry, spray the water…
Slowly, slowly, back to the station…

songs.title: Thank-You Helper Tap (LLH)
songs.motions: Two-finger taps on knees; wave; pretend to write a thank-you card.
songs.teacherDirections: Use before Thank-You Card Workshop and Helper Interview Circle. Collect child ideas for who to thank.
songs.whenToUse: Midweek gratitude focus; transition into writing/art.
songs.transitionPurpose: Moves from dramatic play into gratitude making.
songs.lyrics:
Tap, tap, thank you—helpers near,
Tap, tap, thank you—helpers here.
We see your tools, we learn your job,
Thank you helpers in our neighborhood hub!

Write a card or wave hello,
Helpers help our kindness grow.

songs.title: Mail Carrier March (LLH)
songs.motions: March with pretend mailbag; knock in air; big smile wave.
songs.teacherDirections: Lead into Mail Carrier Center. Use children’s names on envelopes for literacy connection.
songs.whenToUse: Before mail center or block city delivery routes.
songs.suggestedPace: Medium march; one chorus plus name deliveries.
songs.transitionPurpose: Frames delivery jobs and literacy play.
songs.lyrics:
March, march, mail bag on my side,
Letters, letters, we can deliver with pride.
Knock knock—hello!—a smile we bring,
Helpers help with every little thing.

teacherTips: Model once, then narrate what you notice.

teacherToolkit.mixedAgeAdaptations: Offer a simpler parallel tray for younger friends and a design challenge for older preschoolers.
teacherToolkit.extraSupportAdaptations: Sit beside, shorten the invitation, and offer hand-under-hand only when welcomed.
teacherToolkit.challengeExtensions: Invite children to invent a new Community Helpers rule, map, or story for peers.
teacherToolkit.safetyInclusionNotes: Differentiate from toddler unit: preschoolers use maps, interviews, and multi-step dramatic play—still keep props large and roles flexible. No real tools with sharp edges; plastic only. Avoid scary emergency talk; frame firefighters/police as community helpers who practice safety. Mixed-age: remove small mail beads or tiny prop pieces; supervise obstacle courses for spacing. Allergy awareness in Chef’s Kitchen (play food only unless taste test is separately planned with permissions). Thank-you workshops: child-safe scissors and washable glue.
teacherToolkit.endOfWeekReflection: Which Community Helpers words and strategies showed up most in play?
teacherToolkit.familyConnection: Share one Community Helpers word or song to try at home during ordinary routines.
teacherToolkit.notes: Draft toolkit for owner review — enrichment draft only.

legacySnapshot.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers will learn about community helpers who keep neighborhoods safe, healthy, and running smoothly. Through dramatic play, books, movement, and cooperative activities, children explore helper roles, tools, and ways to thank people who help.
legacySnapshot.objectives:
Name several community helpers and describe their jobs
Use helper vocabulary during pretend play
Practice cooperation and problem-solving
Build gratitude language for helpers
Explore tools helpers use safely
Connect helpers to places in the community
